verdict_reason: Three of the four formulas are exact. On a 120x16 cloud, effective_rank matches an independent exp(-sum p log p) on the centered raw spectrum at 0.000e+00, participation_ratio matches (sum L)^2/sum(L^2) at 1.78e-15, and avg_cosine_similarity matches a BRUTE-FORCE all-ordered-distinct-pair Gram average at 3.90e-18; all three are constant across scales 1e-200 to 1e+150 and survive an exact zero-padding isometry d=8 -> 128 to <= 4.7e-13. YELLOW is for cond_number, a FIRST-CLASS output: its numerical-rank cut-off is S[0]*max(shape)*eps(_stored_dtype), but collect_hidden_states already casts hidden states to float32 (utils.py:315/353) so _stored_dtype is ALWAYS float32 and the true stored precision is erased. Production runs dtype=bfloat16 (config.model_args = 'pretrained=...,dtype=bfloat16'), and the same model in the two dtypes then reports cond_number 19.811127663 (fp32) vs 449.643167800 (bf16) on pythia-70m -- 22.7x -- and 24.166894336 vs 629.738056415 on pythia-160m -- 26.1x. Synthetic anchor: an EXACT rank-3 cloud in 16 dimensions stored in bfloat16 reports _meta_numerical_rank = 16 and cond_number = 4167.37 against a true rank 3 and cond 2.13227.
comparable_reason: effective_rank and participation_ratio are dimension counts. Under an iid no-structure null at fixed N = 1000, effective_rank rises 7.988252 -> 31.867887 -> 125.876171 -> 472.649660 for d = 8/32/128/512 (59x) and participation_ratio 7.909716 -> 337.710135, with no change in the underlying geometry; dividing by d does NOT fix it (er/d = 0.998532 / 0.995871 / 0.983408 / 0.923144). They also depend on the realized point count: at fixed d = 64, effective_rank goes 53.239899 -> 63.894403 and cond_number 66.462456 -> 1.247179 (53x) as N goes 70 -> 5000, and defaults.yaml pins num_samples = 100 DOCUMENTS, not points. avg_cosine_similarity is the one comparable output (-0.000267 -> -0.000067 across the same 64x width sweep; on real models 0.9152829646 gpt2, 0.9128960292 distilgpt2, 0.9844522433 pythia-70m, 0.9776329178 pythia-160m).
github_reason: Cloned kawine/contextual and read analyze.py's explore_embedding_space, which defines the published anisotropy: sample 1000 sentences, take ONE random word occurrence from each, then average the cosine over 1000 random pairs. I could not run the released pipeline end to end -- it needs AllenNLP, HDF5 embeddings and the original ~25,573-sentence corpus (word2sent.json indexes up to sentence 25572) while the repo ships only a 98-row sts.csv sample. I therefore reimplemented its sampler and ran BOTH on the same GPT-2 last-layer vectors: released-style 1000-pair Monte Carlo 0.971272703 vs BLME's exact closed form 0.971305979 (delta 3.3e-05), confirming BLME's O(N*D) identity E_{i!=j}[u_i.u_j] = (N||m||^2 - 1)/(N - 1) reproduces the reference estimator.
paper_reason: The released kawine/contextual/gpt2/embedding_space_stats.json publishes 'mean cosine similarity across words' = 0.978 for GPT-2 layer_12 (Ethayarajh 2019 Fig. 1). Running BLME's avg_cosine_similarity kernel on the REFERENCE's own protocol -- one random token per sentence over the 198 sentences shipped in the repo's sts.csv -- gives 0.971305979, relative error -0.68%. The residual is corpus sampling, not the estimator: the released Monte-Carlo estimator on the identical vectors gives 0.971272703, and BLME's own all-token protocol on the same texts gives 0.970524765.
confounds_reason: Causal, by intervention rather than correlation: an iid Gaussian null with IDENTICAL structure at fixed N = 1000 moves effective_rank 7.988252 -> 472.649660 and participation_ratio 7.909716 -> 337.710135 purely by changing d from 8 to 512, and the /d twin still slopes (0.998532 -> 0.923144). Sample size is a second confound: cond_number falls 66.462456 -> 1.247179 over N = 70 -> 5000 at fixed d = 64. On four real models (n = 4, indicative) r(cond_number, d_model) = +0.5548 and r(avg_cosine_similarity, d_model) = -0.6343, but avg_cosine_similarity is flat under the controlled null, so its real-model spread (0.913-0.984) is family structure rather than width.
defects: CODE, VALUE-CHANGING, isotropy.py:~136: rel_tol = S[0]*max(X.shape)*np.finfo(_stored_dtype).eps, but _stored_dtype is read off an array that collect_hidden_states (utils.py:315/353/470) has ALREADY cast to float32, so a bfloat16 run silently uses float32's eps. The shipped configuration is dtype=bfloat16, and the resulting cond_number is 449.643167800 vs 19.811127663 on pythia-70m (22.7x) and 629.738056415 vs 24.166894336 on pythia-160m (26.1x) for the same model, same corpus, same code. gpt2/distilgpt2 are almost unaffected (621.479 vs 620.102, 0.22%), so the impact is model-dependent, not universal.

COMPARABILITY: effective_rank and participation_ratio are raw dimension counts (7.988252 -> 472.649660 over d = 8 -> 512 under a no-structure null) and additionally track the realized point count, which defaults.yaml does not pin (num_samples = 100 DOCUMENTS).

PROTOCOL/CODE, isotropy.py:~395: layerwise = true SILENTLY degrades to the single-layer path when no populated cache is supplied -- measured: the same 2-layer model and 12-document corpus returns 0 layer_metrics entries without a cache and 2 with one, with no error and no flag. defaults.yaml pins layerwise: false, so this never fires in production.

DEMOTED OUTPUT: _meta_svd_auc integrates the cumulative explained-variance curve over its own unpadded length, so an exact zero-padding isometry d = 8 -> 128 moves it 0.550221881 -> 0.971888868 (+76.6%) while every other output is unchanged to <= 4.7e-13. The demotion to _meta_ is correct. It also underflows to NaN at a global scale of 1e-200 (cumsum of S**2), where every promoted output is still exact.

PROVENANCE: participation_ratio has NO cited source in either the code or task_metadata.py:70 (which credits only Ethayarajh 2019 and Roy & Vetterli 2007). It is the standard inverse-participation-ratio / order-2 Hill number of the covariance spectrum, and should be attributed as such.

PROTOCOL/ADAPTATION (disclosed): Ethayarajh's released procedure samples ONE word occurrence per sentence, while BLME uses every token. On the same 198 STS sentences that is 0.971305979 (one per sentence) vs 0.970524765 (all 1,975 tokens); on longer WikiText passages the gap is larger, so the two populations should not be pooled.
fix: (1) Thread the TRUE stored dtype through to _svd_metrics_for_layer -- either have collect_hidden_states report it alongside the tensor, or take it from model.dtype -- so the numerical-rank cut-off uses bfloat16's eps on a bfloat16 run; without that, cond_number is 22.7x-26.1x off on pythia at the shipped dtype. Add the exact rank-3 bf16 regression (currently rank 16, cond 4167.37 against a true rank 3, cond 2.13227). (2) Report the realized point count next to effective_rank / participation_ratio and only pool them at matched N and d, or restrict cross-model comparison to avg_cosine_similarity. (3) Make layerwise = true without a populated cache an explicit error rather than a silent single-layer fallback. (4) Attribute participation_ratio to a source. (5) Keep _meta_svd_auc demoted (+76.6% under a zero-padding isometry).
